subject: Bluejay SLA baseline & monthly-credit trigger (template negotiation)
messages:
From: Dmitri Kuznetsov <dmitri@bluejay.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluejay.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA baseline adjustment + monthly credit cap

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Bluejay has an active safety/regulatory integration with several on-prem sites that necessitate occasional scheduled infra maintenance windows that can cause brief service interruptions for inference traffic we route through Redwood. Our procurement and compliance teams are asking whether Redwood will consider a limited SLA template exception for our account. Specifically: 

- Baseline uptime: 99.5% (vs. Redwood standard 99.9%) for the first 12 months of the contract while integrations stabilize.
- Monthly service credit cap: allow a fixed cap equal to 10% of monthly invoice (our budget constraint).
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance windows announced 72 hours in advance should be excluded from uptime calculations.

I've attached a short request doc outlining the ask (Bluejay_SLA_Request_20260623.pdf). Can your team review and let me know next steps? We're pushing for signature by mid-July.

Appreciate it—
Dmitri
Dmitri Kuznetsov
Head of Procurement, Bluejay Health
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Dmitri Kuznetsov <dmitri@bluejay.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA baseline adjustment + monthly credit cap

Dmitri—

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. Looping in Ben (acct exec) and Marissa (legal) so we can scope the ask from commercial and legal sides. Quick notes from me: 

- We can be flexible on a temporary baseline during an integration/pilot period, but we typically require defined measurement windows and a clear set of maintenance notification requirements.
- 10% monthly cap is higher than our standard allowances in similar deals; we usually propose a lower cap (or a tiered cap tied to severity bands).

Ben/Marissa — can you look and propose a counter-proposal the week of 6/28? Dmitri, if you have a list of the typical maintenance cadence (expected number & duration per month) that would be helpful.

Next steps: Ben will propose commercial guardrails; Marissa will start a redline on the template and highlight carveouts we need.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Dmitri Kuznetsov <dmitri@bluejay.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: SLA baseline adjustment + monthly credit cap

Dmitri—

Appreciate the heads-up and the doc. Based on similar pilots, here's a pragmatic counter we can move quickly on: 

- Pilot baseline: 99.6% for the first 6 months (we'll reassess at the 6-month review).
- Monthly credit cap: 5% of monthly invoice. Alternatively, we can do a tiered credit schedule where small incidents (availability 99.0–99.6) trigger lower credits and severe outages (below 99.0) scale higher, up to 8% in extreme cases.
- Maintenance carveouts: we can accept scheduled maintenance carveouts if Bluejay provides >=7 days notice and a posted maintenance window.

I've attached an initial amendment draft for your review: SLA_Amendment_draft_v1.docx. The key open items for us: exact definition of measurement periods (UTC daily aggregation? monthly calendar days?), and whether Bluejay requires a regulatory audit log (if so, we may need to include an addendum on retention).

If that sounds reasonable, Marissa will send redlines against our template and we can iterate.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Dmitri Kuznetsov <dmitri@bluejay.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluejay.ai, contracts@bluejay.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RE: Request: SLA baseline adjustment + monthly credit cap

Ben/Soojin—

Thanks for the fast turnaround. A few clarifications from procurement: 

- Maintenance cadence: typically 1–2 short windows/month (30–90 minutes each) for edge router/firmware updates during onboarding months; frequency should reduce after 3 months.
- Measurement: we prefer calendar-month aggregation measured in UTC; monthly invoices are calendar months so aligning measurement makes reconciliation easier.
- Credit cap: the 5% cap is lower than internal allowance but the tiered approach is acceptable if the upper bound is clarified. Would Redwood consider a 6% absolute cap (compromise)?

We reviewed the amendment draft and added inline comments in the Drive folder (linked). Procurement is sensitive to blackout windows for reporting—they want a clean, auditable formula for credit calculation.

Dmitri
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Dmitri Kuznetsov <dmitri@bluejay.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: RE: Request: SLA baseline adjustment + monthly credit cap

Dmitri/Team—

Attached are our redlines to the SLA template (Redline_SLA_Bluejay_20260623.pdf). High level: 

- Credit calc: we propose a deterministic formula: (1 - (total_uptime_minutes / total_calendar_minutes)) * monthly_fee. This formula yields transparent, auditable credits and avoids discretionary adjustments.
- Cap: we can move to a 6% absolute cap for the first 6 months, conditional on Bluejay providing >=7 days notice for scheduled maintenance and a run-rate report after month 3. After month 6 we will re-evaluate baseline and cap.
- Measurement windows: UTC calendar-month aggregation OK. We will include an appendix that defines how partial-day maintenance windows are attributed.
- Exclusions: force majeure and customer-side network outages remain carveouts, but we need clear definitions to avoid disputes.

Please review the redlines; if Bluejay accepts the deterministic formula and the 6% cap for the pilot period we can move to execution and attach the amendment to the MSA. Connor from Ops is on cc and can confirm metric reporting feasibility.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Dmitri Kuznetsov <dmitri@bluejay.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RE: RE: Request: SLA baseline adjustment + monthly credit cap

Dmitri—

Quick summary and proposed path to sign: 

- Pilot terms: 99.6% baseline for first 6 months; deterministic credit formula as provided by Marissa; absolute cap of 6% of monthly invoice during pilot.
- Maintenance carveouts: >=7 days notice required for scheduled maintenance to be excluded. Bluejay to provide expected cadence as described (1–2 windows/month, 30–90 minutes) and we will document in the amendment.
- Measurement: UTC calendar-month aggregation. Ops confirms reporting and transparency.

If Bluejay agrees, we'll finalize the amendment, route to DocuSign, and aim to have an executed amendment within 7 business days. Ben will follow up to align on pricing and any concession language for the pilot.

Would you like a short call tomorrow (30 min) to close open items?

Thanks all—
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123
